daily_brief: The day's most consequential developments center on escalating conflicts and diplomatic standoffs. In Yemen, government forces have withdrawn from strategic positions near the Bab al-Mandab Strait to defend the interim capital Aden from advancing Houthi fighters, a move that could reshape the war's trajectory [BBC, Al Jazeera]. Iran announced it will block IAEA inspectors from accessing its damaged nuclear facilities until US conditions are met, following last year's strikes that killed Supreme Leader Khamenei [France 24]. Ukraine launched its largest drone barrage of the war—over 1,300 drones—striking targets including a key Crimea bridge, while Russia claimed to intercept most of them [Le Monde, Globe and Mail]. In Europe, five EU nations are expected to announce a pilot migrant deportation center in Rwanda, testing a new approach to asylum policy [BBC]. At COP31 in Turkey, Australia released a draft deal calling for 'accelerated action' to phase out fossil fuels, though significant gaps remain among negotiating parties [The Hindu, RFI]. Meanwhile, attention turns to this week's Trump-Xi meeting at the APEC summit, though analysts suggest substantive breakthroughs on trade or security are unlikely [Globe and Mail, Nikkei Asia].

top_stories.headline: Yemen Government Forces Withdraw from Bab al-Mandab to Defend Aden from Houthi Advance
bullets: Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces announced withdrawal from Dhubab Airport and territory near the Bab al-Mandab Strait to reinforce positions around Aden, Yemen's interim capital
Houthi forces have claimed control of evacuated territory, including areas seized in a September offensive such as Perim Island and the port city of Mokha
Fighting now centers on a strategic triangle linking Aden, the besieged city of Taiz, and the Bab al-Mandab maritime chokepoint connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden
Military analysts describe this triangle as the 'strategic centre of gravity' that could determine the war's outcome

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Focuses on military redeployment as defensive measure, notes Saudi Arabia has not commented

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Emphasizes Houthi advances and includes expert analysis on strategic implications, frames situation as 'potentially catastrophic' for government forces

top_stories.headline: Iran Blocks UN Nuclear Inspectors Until US Meets Conditions for Ending Middle East War
bullets: Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi announced Iran will deny IAEA access to damaged nuclear facilities until Iranian conditions are met and the war has 'permanently ended'
Nuclear site inspections have been suspended since last year's 12-day war with Israel, during which US strikes also hit Iranian nuclear facilities
IAEA inspectors visited Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant in September but have been denied access to bombed sites including Natanz, Fordow, and Isfahan
The statement follows IAEA calls for Tehran to resume inspections; Iranian facilities were hit again during the February 2026 war that killed Supreme Leader Khamenei

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Straightforward reporting on Iranian official statements, includes context on previous US-Israeli strikes

top_stories.headline: Ukraine Launches Record 1,300-Drone Barrage, Strikes Key Crimea Bridge
bullets: Russia's Defence Ministry claimed to intercept 1,336 Ukrainian drones, the highest number since the 2022 invasion began
Ukrainian forces struck a key bridge in Crimea and hit oil depots in Russia's Rostov region, working with pro-Kyiv insurgents inside Russia
Six people were wounded in Russia's Krasnodar region and three in Azov city; approximately 600 drones targeted the Moscow region
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas accused Putin of making 'maximalist demands' to extend the conflict as US-mediated talks remain stalled

sources.name: Le Monde
sources.framing_note: Headlines emphasize Ukrainian offensive capability and Crimea bridge strike

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Provides broader context on US-mediated talks and war casualties

sources.framing_note: Leads with Russian attacks killing civilians, frames through EU diplomatic criticism of Moscow

top_stories.headline: Five EU Nations to Announce Migrant Deportation Center in Rwanda
bullets: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece, and the Netherlands are expected to announce creation of a migrant deportation hub in Rwanda on Monday in Vienna
Unlike the scrapped UK scheme, this would apply only to asylum seekers who have exhausted legal avenues to remain in the EU
The pilot program would initially host approximately 100 people, with each country potentially sending about 20 migrants
Human rights bodies warn the plan could violate migrant rights, though the five countries insist it complies with EU and international law

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Balanced reporting noting both government justifications and human rights concerns, provides context on failed UK precedent

top_stories.headline: COP31 Draft Deal Calls for Accelerated Fossil Fuel Phaseout Amid Finance Disputes
bullets: Australia released first draft of COP31 political agreement calling for 'accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels' in energy systems
Draft expresses 'deep concern' over impending breach of Paris Agreement's 1.5°C target and affirms IPCC science
Text calls for tripling climate adaptation finance for developing countries to at least $120 billion annually
Significant gaps remain among nearly 200 nations with consensus deal due by Friday; summit closes November 20 in Antalya, Turkey

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Detailed coverage of draft text specifics and developing country demands
